 Entersekt strengthens 3-D Secure to help merchants, banks convert more holiday sales
 Entersekt strengthens 3-D Secure to help merchants, banks convert more holiday sales
 Issued by Entersekt Stellenbosch, SA, 30 Oct 2026 Turning genuine purchases into revenue. Entersekt , which positions itself as a global leader in digital banking fraud prevention and online payment security, today announced enhancements to its 3-D Secure (3DS) offering to help merchants and issuers turn more genuine purchases into revenue ahead of the holiday shopping peak. 
 When authentication gets stuck, the shopper who wanted to buy is lost, and with them the merchant’s sale and the issuer’s interchange. In early adopter deployments of the enhancements, however, net authentication success rates rose by up to 9.0 percentage points. When a shopper’s browser failed after authentication, results were still delivered for about 3% of authenticated transactions, worth approximately R7 million ($423 000) (1) over seven days, which would otherwise never have reached the merchant.
 “An authentication that succeeds but never reaches the merchant still leaves the customer unable to complete a purchase,” says Dewald Nolte , Co-Founder and Chief Product Strategy and Market Engagement Officer at Entersekt. “The shopper does everything right: they approve the purchase with their bank, close the app and assume they’re done. If that result never reaches the merchant, the purchase never completes. Our enhancements make sure the result still gets through, so a broken handoff doesn’t cost the sale.” 
 Closing the gap between authentication and checkout
 Online card payments can involve several steps: a customer begins checkout with a merchant, switches to a banking app or authentication page to confirm the purchase, and returns to the merchant to complete the payment. Browser interruptions, page reloads or unreliable connections can break this sequence at different stages.
 The enhancements made by Entersekt apply to the company’s access control server (ACS) and 3DS Server (3DSS). ACS enhancements improve the resilience of cardholder authentication when browser interactions are interrupted. 3DSS enhancements help preserve completed authentication results for delivery to the merchant when the expected browser return fails.
 Together, the capabilities address two distinct failure points in the 3DS journey, helping issuers, merchants and payment service providers (PSPs) reduce avoidable checkout disruptions for their customers. 
 “Our production results demonstrate how interruptions at different stages of authentication can affect payment continuity, even when the purchase is legitimate and the cardholder successfully played their part. They also highlight why resilience needs to extend beyond the authentication step itself,” says Nolte. “For merchants and the PSPs that serve them, an authentication only pays off once the result arrives, because that’s when the sale can go ahead. That’s the moment we built these enhancements to protect.”
 Timing is everything
 South Africa’s online retail sector is expected to reach R159 billion in 2026, growing by 22.5% and accounting for an average of 10% of national retail turnover, according to the Online Retail in South Africa 2026 report. With 57.9% of online shoppers using smartphones to shop, reliable checkout experiences across mobile browsers and banking apps are increasingly important, particularly during the busy festive shopping period.
 “During peak shopping periods, every completed purchase counts. When a legitimate payment fails because of a technical problem during checkout, merchants can lose sales that customers were ready to make. As digital shopping grows and payment journeys get more complex, checkout reliability matters more to conversion,” says Serpil Hall , Strategic Advisor, Fraud and AML at Datos Insights . “Making sure the authentication result reaches the merchant, even when something interrupts the journey, is a practical step towards protecting revenue and giving customers the smooth experience they expect.” 
 Entersekt is making the enhancements available to eligible customers, subject to supported configurations and activation requirements. Banks, merchants and PSPs can contact Entersekt for further information.
 (1) The production results were measured in separate deployments in the United States. The $423 000 (approximately R7 million at the time of publication) represents authenticated transaction value preserved for further processing, not confirmed completed purchases or recognised revenue.

 Entersekt provides financial institutions with digital banking fraud prevention and payment security solutions through its cross-channel, Context Aware™ Authentication platform that secures digital transactions and optimizes user experiences. Founded in 2010, Entersekt serves financial institutions around the world and holds 120+ patents for its security innovations. In 2023, Entersekt acquired the Modirum 3-D Secure software business from Modirum, a security technology firm based in Helsinki, Finland, positioning Entersekt as a global industry leader in authentication solutions for financial services. Entersekt processes 8bn+ transactions for 250m+ cardholders and 450,000+ merchants from nearly 900 banks in 70+ countries. Backed by companies like Silicon Valley-based Accel-KKR, one of the world’s top private equity firms, Entersekt continues to expand its footprint across key regions.
